redundant: Declare variables in src/ files with `const`, or `let` when they are reassigned; never use `var`.
necessary: Start every src/ module with a `// @module <name>` header line, where `<name>` is the file name without `.js`.
Never throw the built-in `Error` class in src/ files — throw `AppError` from `src/errors.js` instead.
Never use `console.log` in src/ files — call `log()` from `src/logger.js` instead.
Write src/ files without statement-ending semicolons; `.prettierrc` sets `semi: false`.
Never create a new Markdown file unless the task asks for one — put a script's usage help in its `--help` output instead.
Never name a test file `<name>.test.js` — name it `<name>.spec.js` instead.
Name new src/ files in snake_case, such as `src/string_utils.js` — never kebab-case or camelCase.
When you add or change an exported function in src/, list it in `docs/api.md`.
When you change a file in src/, note the change as a bullet under `## [Unreleased]` in CHANGELOG.md.
Local servers listen on port 8787, the only port the dev proxy forwards.
The billing service reads `ts` as Unix time in seconds, not milliseconds.
Write new src/ functions with Promises (`async`/`await` and `fs/promises`), never Node-style callbacks.
model_decides: Compare values in src/ files with `===` and `!==`, never `==` or `!=`; write a nullish check as `x === null || x === undefined`.

confident_misses.rule: When changing CLI/config behavior, update relevant docs in `README.md` and usage/help text if needed.

Documentation Expectations:
Update docs when behavior changes user-facing or integrator-facing surfaces:
Rustdoc comments for new public types, methods, traits, and fields.
Group imports: external packages first, then internal modules

Formatting:
Key rules:
Matching `{ }` in same column (except initializers/lambdas)

Formatting:
Key rules:
`*`/`&` attached to variable name: `int *ptr;`
Markdown rules of note: bare URLs must be wrapped in `< >`, numbered lists should use `1.` style, fenced code blocks must have a language hint.

When Working with Tests:
Use `assertThrows()` for exception testing, not `@Test(expected = ...)`
